body: NATO launched a counter-drone marketplace on November 5, 2026, enabling allied countries to order from a catalog of 16 preselected solutions without running a separate tender. The NATO Communications and Information Agency, which manages the marketplace, selected Alta Ares, Axon Enterprise, Northrop Grumman, OSL UK and Quantum Systems; the selected capabilities have already been deployed in allied countries and Ukraine, and include static, transportable and mobile systems to protect military installations, critical infrastructure and troops on the move.

NCIA evaluated bids against four reference scenarios: area protection covering a zone up to 3 kilometers in diameter, such as an airbase or logistics hub; border protection across a 20-kilometer border segment; convoy protection for a moving column up to 300 meters long traveling at up to 50 kilometers per hour; and point protection for a single high-value asset or location such as a command post. The framework contracts run for 18 months from signature, with an option to extend, and NATO has allocated 3.1 million euros ($3.5 million) to fund further testing of the selected systems by allied nations or NATO commands.

French counter-drone company Alta Ares announced on November 5 that it had secured six of the 16 lots, covering area defense and border protection, and was the only supplier selected for area defense across fixed, deployable and mobile configurations; in June 2026 it signed a memorandum of understanding with Airbus Defence and Space to integrate its interceptors into the Fortion IBMS command and control software. The marketplace forms part of Drone Edge, an initiative launched by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte at the NATO Summit Defence Industry Forum in Ankara on July 7, 2026, under which allies committed to investing more than $40 billion (35.6 billion euros) in counter-drone capabilities over five years, although the procurement competition predates Drone Edge: NCIA notified NATO nations of the planned framework on October 17, 2025.
en.summary: NATO launched a counter-drone marketplace on November 5, letting allies order from a catalog of 16 preselected systems without a separate tender; French firm Alta Ares secured six of the 16 lots.

body: 北約於2026年11月5日開設反無人機市集，盟國可直接從16套預選方案的目錄下單，無需另行招標。負責管理市集的北約通訊與資訊局選定Alta Ares、Axon Enterprise、諾斯洛普格拉曼、OSL UK與Quantum Systems等5家廠商；入選系統已在盟國與烏克蘭部署，涵蓋固定式、可運輸式與機動式系統，用於保護軍事設施、關鍵基礎設施與行進中的部隊。

北約通訊與資訊局以4種參考情境評估投標：區域防護涵蓋直徑3公里的範圍，如空軍基地或後勤樞紐；邊境防護涵蓋20公里長的邊境段；車隊防護涵蓋長度300公尺、時速50公里以內的移動車隊；定點防護則針對指揮所或軍事設施等單一高價值目標。框架合約自簽署起為期18個月，可選擇延長；北約通訊與資訊局計畫定期舉辦競標，以跟上無人機與反無人機技術的變化；北約另撥款310萬歐元（350萬美元），資助盟國或北約指揮部進一步測試入選系統。

法國反無人機業者Alta Ares於11月5日宣布取得16個標案中的6個，涵蓋區域防禦與邊境防護，也是唯一在固定式、可部署式與機動式3種構型皆入選區域防禦的供應商；Alta Ares於2026年6月與空中巴士防衛與太空簽署合作備忘錄，將攔截器整合進Fortion IBMS指管軟體。此市集屬於北約秘書長馬克·呂特於2026年7月7日在安卡拉北約峰會國防產業論壇啟動的Drone Edge倡議一環，盟國承諾5年內投入逾400億美元（356億歐元）發展反無人機能力；但此次採購競標早於Drone Edge，北約通訊與資訊局早在2025年10月17日就通知盟國相關框架計畫。
zh.summary: 北約11月5日開設反無人機市集，盟國可直接訂購16套預選系統，涵蓋5家廠商；法國Alta Ares取得其中6個標案。
zh.title: 北約開設反無人機市集，16套系統供盟國免招標採購
